list_child.name: ls_rules
list_child.desc: Returns every alert rule configured in the live alerting engine. Use this to see the full rule set before making any single change.

decoys.name: ls_staged
decoys.desc: Returns every alert rule staged in the rules repository. Use this to see the full set queued for the next config deploy.

decoys.name: ls_synth
decoys.desc: Returns every alert rule configured in the synthetic probe runner. Use this to see the full set of uptime checks before editing any probe.

decoys.name: ls_archived
decoys.desc: Returns every alert rule kept in the rule history archive. Use this to see the full set retired from paging over time.

get_child.name: get_rule
get_child.desc: Retrieves the rule definition for one alert rule by its id. It returns every field currently stored for that rule.

decoys.name: get_hist
decoys.desc: Retrieves the firing history for one alert rule by its id. It returns every trigger and resolve event logged for that rule.

decoys.name: get_runbook
decoys.desc: Retrieves the linked runbook for one alert rule by its id. It returns the response steps written for that rule.

decoys.name: get_escalation
decoys.desc: Retrieves the escalation policy for one alert rule by its id. It returns every responder tier configured for that rule.

list_parent.name: ls_svcs
list_parent.desc: Returns every service registered in the platform's service catalog. Use this to look up a service before inspecting its rules.

decoys.name: ls_traced
decoys.desc: Returns every service registered with the tracing collector. Use this to look up a service before inspecting its spans.

decoys.name: ls_status
decoys.desc: Returns every service registered on the public status page. Use this to look up a service before posting an incident update.

decoys.name: ls_oncall
decoys.desc: Returns every service registered with the on-call scheduler. Use this to look up a service before inspecting its rota.

get_parent.name: get_svc
get_parent.desc: Retrieves the catalog entry for one service by its id. It returns the service's full registered metadata.

decoys.name: get_slo
decoys.desc: Retrieves the SLO targets for one service by its id. It returns the service's availability and latency objectives.

decoys.name: get_rota
decoys.desc: Retrieves the on-call rota for one service by its id. It returns the service's current and next responders.

decoys.name: get_deploys
decoys.desc: Retrieves the deploy log for one service by its id. It returns the service's recent releases and rollbacks.

delete_child.name: rm_rule
delete_child.desc: Deletes an alert rule permanently from the service's configuration. Once removed, the rule is gone for good.

decoys.name: purge_hist
decoys.desc: Deletes an alert rule's firing history permanently from the metrics store. Once purged, the events are gone for good.

decoys.name: drop_runbook
decoys.desc: Deletes an alert rule's linked runbook permanently from the team wiki. Once dropped, the page is gone for good.

decoys.name: close_incidents
decoys.desc: Closes every open incident raised by an alert rule permanently in the tracker. Once closed, the incidents are locked for good.
verbs: shut every open incident raised by {obj}

set_enum.name: set_rule_state
set_enum.desc: Updates a rule's live state to enabled, disabled, firing, or resolved. This overwrites whatever state the rule was previously in.

decoys.name: set_canary_state
decoys.desc: Updates a rule's canary state to enabled, disabled, firing, or resolved. This overwrites whatever state the canary cluster was previously in.

decoys.name: set_drill_state
decoys.desc: Updates a rule's drill state to enabled, disabled, firing, or resolved. This overwrites whatever state the fire drill was previously in.

decoys.name: set_page_state
decoys.desc: Updates a rule's status page state to enabled, disabled, firing, or resolved. This overwrites whatever state the public page was previously in.

set_bool.name: mute_rule
set_bool.desc: Mutes an alert rule so it stops paging on-call. This is meant for rules that are known-noisy or under investigation.

decoys.name: ack_rule
decoys.desc: Acknowledges an alert rule so it stops re-notifying on-call. This is meant for rules that are firing and already being worked.

decoys.name: pin_rule
decoys.desc: Pins an alert rule so it stays at the top of the on-call dashboard. This is meant for rules that need watching during a release.

decoys.name: escalate_rule
decoys.desc: Escalates an alert rule so it pages the secondary on-call. This is meant for rules that went unanswered at the first tier.

set_ref.name: mv_rule
set_ref.desc: Moves an alert rule to a different service. This is used when a rule was configured against the wrong service.

decoys.name: route_rule
decoys.desc: Routes an alert rule's pages to a different service's on-call. This is used when another team is covering that pager for a while.

decoys.name: link_rule
decoys.desc: Links an alert rule to a different service as its upstream dependency. This is used when the rule's failures stem from that service.

decoys.name: cc_rule
decoys.desc: Forwards an alert rule's notifications to a different service's channel. This is used when a downstream team wants to see the rule fire.

send.name: ping_svc
send.desc: Sends a notification about a rule to the service's owning team. This is the standard channel for surfacing an alert rule issue.

decoys.name: page_svc
decoys.desc: Sends a high-urgency page about a rule to the service's on-call engineer. This is the standard channel for waking someone for an outage.

decoys.name: ticket_svc
decoys.desc: Files a ticket about a rule in the service's team backlog. This is the standard channel for low-urgency rule cleanup work.
child_verbs: file a ticket with the owner of {obj}
open a ticket for the owner of {obj}

decoys.name: review_svc
decoys.desc: Sends a postmortem request about a rule to the service's owning team. This is the standard channel for asking for a written incident review.
child_verbs: request a postmortem from the owner of {obj}
ask the owner of {obj} for a postmortem

create.name: new_rule
create.desc: Creates a new alert rule on a service, with an optional condition summary and starting state. Use this when a service needs coverage for a new failure mode.

decoys.name: new_slo
decoys.desc: Creates a new SLO objective on a service, with an optional condition summary and starting state. Use this when a service needs a reliability target tracked.

decoys.name: new_probe
decoys.desc: Creates a new synthetic probe on a service, with an optional condition summary and starting state. Use this when an endpoint needs an outside-in uptime check.

decoys.name: new_panel
decoys.desc: Creates a new dashboard panel on a service, with an optional condition summary and starting state. Use this when a metric needs a chart for the team.

list_notes.name: ls_rule_notes
list_notes.desc: Returns the notes attached to a single alert rule. It includes every remark engineers have logged against that rule.

decoys.name: ls_rule_incs
decoys.desc: Returns the incident timelines attached to a single alert rule. It includes every event responders have logged against that rule.

decoys.name: ls_rule_annos
decoys.desc: Returns the graph annotations attached to a single alert rule. It includes every marker engineers have pinned to that rule's chart.

decoys.name: ls_rule_archived
decoys.desc: Returns the archived notes attached to a single alert rule. It includes every older remark engineers have moved out of view.

add_note.name: add_rule_note
add_note.desc: Attaches a new note to an alert rule, with an optional title. Use this to record remarks from investigation or review.

decoys.name: add_rule_anno
decoys.desc: Pins a new graph annotation to an alert rule, with an optional title. Use this to mark a deploy or outage on the chart.

decoys.name: add_rule_inc
decoys.desc: Logs a new incident timeline entry on an alert rule, with an optional title. Use this to record what responders did and when.

decoys.name: pin_rule_note
decoys.desc: Pins a new note to the top of an alert rule, with an optional title. Use this to flag remarks every responder should read.

update_note.name: edit_rule_note
update_note.desc: Changes the text, and optionally the title, of an existing note on an alert rule. Use this to correct or expand a remark after it has been logged.

decoys.name: edit_rule_anno
decoys.desc: Changes the text, and optionally the title, of an existing graph annotation on an alert rule. Use this to reword a chart marker after it has been pinned.

decoys.name: reply_rule_note
decoys.desc: Posts a reply, and optionally a title, under an existing note on an alert rule. Use this to answer a remark after it has been logged.

decoys.name: append_rule_note
decoys.desc: Appends text, and optionally a new title, to an existing note on an alert rule. Use this to add findings beneath a remark after it has been logged.

delete_note.name: rm_rule_note
delete_note.desc: Permanently removes a note from an alert rule. Once removed, the note is gone for good.

decoys.name: rm_rule_anno
decoys.desc: Permanently removes a graph annotation from an alert rule. Once removed, the marker is gone for good.

decoys.name: redact_rule_note
decoys.desc: Permanently redacts the text of a note on an alert rule. Once redacted, the wording is gone for good.

decoys.name: rm_note_replies
decoys.desc: Permanently removes the replies under a note on an alert rule. Once removed, the thread is gone for good.

set_image.name: set_rule_img
set_image.desc: Sets the image shown on an alert rule. It is typically a graph snapshot of the metric the rule watches.

decoys.name: set_rule_topo
decoys.desc: Sets the topology diagram shown on an alert rule. It is typically a map of the hosts the rule covers.

decoys.name: set_rule_heatmap
decoys.desc: Sets the latency heatmap image shown on an alert rule. It is typically a render of the request spread the rule tracks.

decoys.name: set_rule_flame
decoys.desc: Sets the flame graph shown on an alert rule. It is typically a profile of the code path the rule points at.

writer.name: write_text
writer.desc: Writes a short message from a brief, which states what to say in the requester's own words, and the alert rules it should mention. It returns the finished text.

decoys.name: write_pm
decoys.desc: Writes a short postmortem from a brief, which states what happened in the requester's own words, and the alert rules it should cite. It returns the finished postmortem.

decoys.name: write_update
decoys.desc: Writes a short status page update from a brief, which states what to say in the requester's own words, and the alert rules it should mention. It returns the finished update.

decoys.name: write_runbook
decoys.desc: Writes a short runbook section from a brief, which states the fix in the requester's own words, and the alert rules it should cover. It returns the finished section.

image.name: render_img
image.desc: Generates an image from a text prompt and returns its URL. It accepts an optional visual style for the result.

decoys.name: render_diagram
decoys.desc: Generates an architecture diagram from a text prompt and returns its URL. It accepts an optional visual style for the diagram.

decoys.name: render_chart
decoys.desc: Generates a metrics chart from a text prompt and returns its URL. It accepts an optional visual style for the chart.

decoys.name: render_badge
decoys.desc: Generates a status badge from a text prompt and returns its URL. It accepts an optional visual style for the badge.

search.name: search_docs
search.desc: Searches the help docs and knowledge base with a question and returns the best matching passage. It is the quickest way to look up how the platform works.

decoys.name: search_runbooks
decoys.desc: Searches the runbook docs with a question and returns the best matching passage. It is the quickest way to look up how to respond to an alert.

decoys.name: search_incidents
decoys.desc: Searches the incident archive with a question and returns the best matching passage. It is the quickest way to look up how a past outage was handled.

decoys.name: search_qref
decoys.desc: Searches the query language knowledge base with a question and returns the best matching passage. It is the quickest way to look up a metric function's syntax.
